name: Shillong
description: Capital city of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district. Known as the 'Scotland of the East', it sits at about 1,500 m elevation with colonial architecture, markets, educational institutions, and access to nearby waterfalls and peaks.
facts: Capital and largest city of Meghalaya
HQ of East Khasi Hills district
Connected by road to Guwahati (about 100 km)

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at approximately 1,965 m, about 10 km south of Shillong city. Offers panoramic views of the city, surrounding hills, and on clear days the Bangladesh plains. Sacred site for local Khasi people with a shrine to U Lei Shillong.
facts: Highest peak in Meghalaya at about 1965 m
Indian Air Force radar station area; ID required

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, about 12 km from the city centre. Locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Named after an elephant-shaped rock (destroyed in 1897 earthquake) that once stood nearby.
facts: Three successive falls over fern-covered rocks
Original Khasi name means three-step waterfall

name: Ward's Lake
description: Man-made horseshoe-shaped lake in central Shillong, also known as Nan Polok or Pollock's Lake. Built in 1894 under Sir William Ward, surrounded by botanical gardens, cobblestone paths, a wooden bridge, and boating facilities.
facts: Popular for morning walks and boating

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Major museum and research centre in Mawlai, Shillong, showcasing the cultures, artefacts, and lifestyles of Northeast India's indigenous peoples across 19 galleries. Includes a skywalk and specialised library.

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Historic town on the southern plateau of East Khasi Hills, formerly the wettest place on Earth. Gateway to dramatic waterfalls, limestone caves, living root bridges, and deep gorges overlooking the Bangladesh plains.
facts: Once recorded as wettest place on Earth
Sub-division HQ in East Khasi Hills
Base for Nohkalikai Falls and root bridges

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m, located near Sohra. Drops from the plateau edge into a turquoise pool amid steep cliffs and forests. Named after a local legend of a woman who jumped from the cliff.
facts: Fed by plateau rainfall; turquoise plunge pool

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented waterfall near Mawsmai village, dropping over 300 m in seven parallel streams down limestone cliffs. Also known as Seven Sisters Falls, spectacular during monsoons.

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone show cave near Sohra, about 150 m of lit passages with stalactites and stalagmites. First electrified show cave in Meghalaya; easy for visitors of all ages.
facts: Name means 'Oath Stone Cave' in Khasi

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Unique two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, formed by guiding aerial roots of Ficus elastica trees across a stream over centuries by the Khasi people. Requires a trek of about 3,500 steps from Tyrna.
facts: Two stacked levels of living roots
Trek of roughly 3000-3500 steps from Tyrna

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Village near the India-Bangladesh border known as Asia's cleanest village. Features bamboo dustbins, living root bridges at nearby Riwai, skywalk, and community-led cleanliness practices among the Khasi people.
facts: Declared cleanest village in Asia in 2003 by Discover India
In Pynursla block near Bangladesh border

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon viewpoint about 25 km from Shillong near Smit. Offers sweeping views of deep gorges, ridges, and valleys, popular for photography and short hikes.
facts: Also known as Laitlum Grand Canyon

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove near Mawphlang village, protected for centuries by Khasi traditional beliefs. Biodiversity hotspot with old-growth trees, orchids, and monoliths; nothing may be removed from the forest.
facts: Rich in endemic flora and orchids

name: Kongthong Whistling Village
description: Remote village in East Khasi Hills where residents use unique whistled tunes as names. Features living root bridges, trekking trails, and eco-tourism amid forested hills.
facts: In East Khasi Hills near Sohra region
